$schema_note: Facts about the relate CLI for the docs pipeline (DOCS-PLAN.md §8 check 3, the <ExitCodes>/<Flags>/<EnvVars> components). Summaries are paraphrases; strings in `messages` and in backticks are quoted from the binary or the sources character for character. Facts the sources disagreed on were settled against the binary named in `recorded_with` (`settled_by`); before launch that is a source build, not a published release (engine.json `source_build`). `verify` marks what the binary cannot show. `recorded` holds a replayable run of the binary (see `recording`); `help` and `agent_context` hold the recorded `--help` pages and agent briefings.

commands.summary: Run a statement session: one statement or a `;`-separated list (positional or `-c`), a script on piped stdin, or the interactive shell on a terminal. Takes every query-run flag.
commands.note: The path-first form with no statement (`relate --database ./s.rl < script.cypher`) prints the top-level help on piped or redirected stdin and exits 0; a script on stdin needs `relate query`.

Usage: relate [OPTIONS] [--database PATH] [QUERY]

Commands:
  query          Run a statement session (oneshot, stdin, or shell)
  clone          Copy a database into a new store and exit
  info           Print store metadata for a database without opening it
  pull           Copy a Neo4j/Aura subgraph into a database
  push           Copy a database subgraph into Neo4j/Aura
  skill          Install, inspect, or remove the embedded agent skill bundle
  upgrade        Update the relate binary (alias: update)
  telemetry      Manage anonymous usage metrics (on, off, status)
  run            Run an installed extension action into a store the host owns
  serve          Host the HTTP Query API and MCP surfaces on a database
  agent-context  Print the compact agent briefing (commands, flags, exit codes)
  extension      Scaffold, install, check, list, or remove command extensions

Options:
  -h, --help    Show this help and exit
  --version     Show version and license and exit (with --json: one JSON object)
  -d, --database PATH  Database directory, .rl bundle, or :memory: (default :memory:)
                       The store to open — never a URL: a remote store is a --load
                       source
  --json        Output as JSON (indented on a terminal, compact when piped)
  --csv         Output as CSV
  --markdown    Output as Markdown
  --jsonl       Output as JSON Lines
  --toon        Output as TOON (one header line, one line per row)
  --noheader    Disable column headers
  --mode MODE   Set output mode (table, csv, json, jsonl, envelope, markdown, cypher, toon, speedscope)
                default: table on a terminal, jsonl when stdout is piped or redirected
                (toon instead of jsonl when agent mode is on)
  --format MODE Alias of --mode
  --pretty      Indent JSON output even when stdout is not a terminal
  --param N=V   Bind a Cypher parameter (repeatable; V parsed as JSON scalar, bare words are strings)
  --fetch-params N=SRC  Fetch a URL or read a file (http, https, file path), parse it as JSON, and bind it as the parameter N (repeatable)
  --snapshot-format F  Snapshot codec (parquet|json|markdown); empty directory only
  --markdown-body-properties LIST  Markdown vault body properties (LIST or
                       Label=LIST; entries separated by ';'; first bare, rest as
                       ## sections; default: body)
  --wal-dir DIR        WAL directory (default <DATABASE>/wal)
  --checkpoint-interval-secs N  Timed checkpoint period; 0 disables
  --durability-mode MODE  WAL durability (full|everysecond|snapshot; default full,
                       RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE)
  --logical-graph-size-limit SIZE  Live graph + index cap (bytes or mb/mib/gb/gib)
  --expression-memory-limit SIZE  Per-value expression build cap (bytes, mb/mib/gb/gib, or none)
                       Default: 256 MiB. Guards against one statement
                       building a pathological single value; raise it, or
                       pass none for known bulk pipelines
  --concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE  Shared logical-workspace pool (bytes or mb/mib/gb/gib)
                       A positive value turns admission on. Omit, or an
                       unset RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT,
                       leaves it off. 0 is rejected
  --max-traversal-depth N  Largest explicit traversal hop bound (1-2000; default 500)
                       A query whose explicit hop bound exceeds this fails at
                       admission with TraversalDepthExceeded. This is a safety
                       limit, not a database limit: raising it risks a stack
                       overflow on small-stack platforms.
                       RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH sets the default
  --safe               Refuse agent-typical dangerous statement shapes; --no-safe
                       negates it. Refuses a new named node without a label, and
                       a MATCH read without LIMIT or a reducing aggregate
                       (collect() does not count). A policy, not a database
                       limit. RELATE_SAFE_MODE=1/0 sets the default; off
                       unless asked.
  --agent-mode         Force agent ergonomics on (the row cap's default and the
                       toon piped default); pairs with --max-rows.
                       --no-agent-mode turns them off (the -mode suffix stays
                       clear of the skill-install harness selector).
                       Precedence: the flag, then RELATE_AGENT_MODE=1/0,
                       then harness detection (piped runs only). The explicit
                       acts print a one-line announcement; detection stays silent
  --max-rows N         Print at most N rows per statement; 0 = unlimited.
                       Default: 100 under a detected agent harness with stdout
                       not a terminal, unlimited otherwise (RELATE_MAX_ROWS)
  --width N            Wrap the human table to N display columns; the widest
                       columns shrink and their cells wrap over lines.
                       Default: the terminal width, else an exported COLUMNS
                       (both floored at 20), else the natural width
  --timeout DURATION   Cancel a statement that runs longer (500ms, 10s, 2m;
                       bare number = seconds; 0 disables). Exit code 7
  --load SOURCE        Load a store's content from a .rl path, a directory, or an
                       https URL. With :memory: (the default target) the source is
                       turned into the in-memory store: a read-only open that releases
                       the source after the load (nothing is held open or locked, so
                       it can be deleted or opened writable underneath). With a
                       --database path the source is cloned there and the store opens
                       normally (the target must not exist yet). --read-only=live is
                       refused
                       An https URL is fetched to a private temp copy — a GitHub blob
                       or raw link is rewritten to its raw form; a remote folder store
                       is not supported. Nothing is kept: the memory target releases
                       the copy after the load, a path target removes it after the
                       clone
  --read-only[=FRESH]  Open an existing database without writing or checkpointing.
                       FRESH is snapshot (default: a frozen snapshot at open) or
                       live (tail the WAL and follow the writer's commits;
                       refused for .rl and :memory:). Attach the value
                       (--read-only=live); once per run.
                       A native directory can be open beside a writer. A .rl file
                       opens only while no writer holds it. :memory: rejects writes
                       and creates nothing
  --load-csv-dir PATH  Allow local LOAD CSV under this directory (default denied; overrides RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR)
  --namespace NAME     Session namespace (neo4j|system|system_ontologies; default neo4j)
  -c, --command Q      One-shot statement or `;`-separated list (same as positional QUERY)
  --            Treat all following arguments as positional
On a TTY, the interactive shell supports readline-style editing (arrow keys, Home/End).

--database is a directory (WAL + snapshot), a .rl bundle, or :memory: (the default).
With no QUERY, the interactive shell opens on a terminal; on piped
or redirected stdin this help is printed. `query` with no STATEMENT reads a script
from stdin, or opens the same shell on a terminal.

  relate --database ./mydata --json -c "MATCH (n) RETURN count(n) AS nodes"
  # Explore without being able to change anything
  relate --database ./mydata --read-only --mode envelope -c "MATCH (n:Person) RETURN n.name LIMIT 5"

Usage: relate pull [--from FILE] --query Q [--param N=V] [--allow-plaintext] --database PATH

  --query Q     Cypher statement, `;`-separated statement list, file path, or `-` (stdin);
               every statement must RETURN graph elements; all run in one process,
               one checkpoint at the end
  -d, --database PATH  Destination directory or .rl bundle (required; not :memory:)
  --param N=V   Bind a source query parameter (repeatable)
  --allow-plaintext  Permit Basic auth to a non-loopback http:// Query API
                     (insecure; prints a warning); default off

  # Copy a Neo4j/Aura subgraph into a local database
  relate pull --from .env --query 'MATCH (n)-[r]->(m) RETURN n, r, m LIMIT 100' --database ./graph

Usage: relate push --to CREDS --database PATH [--query Q | --labels L1,L2 | --types T1,T2] [--batch-size N] [--nodes-update POLICY] [--rels-update POLICY] [--updated-at NAME[,NAME]] [--rel-mode MODE] [--merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]] [--rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]] [--unkeyed-labels ACTION] [--dry-run] [--json] [--allow-plaintext]

push copies a scoped subgraph of --database into a Neo4j/Aura remote over
HTTP Query API v2 — pull's mirror, over the same client.
  --to CREDS   Env file (NEO4J_URI, NEO4J_USERNAME, NEO4J_PASSWORD, optional
               NEO4J_DATABASE), or a Query API URI (username/password then
               come from the process environment)
  -d, --database PATH  Source store directory or .rl bundle (required; not :memory:)
  --query Q    Only what the statements RETURN (nodes/rels/paths; a `;`-list,
               file path, or `-` for stdin). One of --query/--labels/--types;
               none pushes the whole store
  --labels L1,L2  Only nodes with these labels, and the rels between them
  --types T1,T2   Only rels of these types, with both their endpoints
  --batch-size N   Rows per batched statement (default 5000)
  --nodes-update POLICY  add (default) | replace | skip, per label or global
               (Movie=replace,Person=skip). add: SET += keeps remote-only
               properties; replace: SET = overwrites; skip: create missing only
  --rels-update POLICY  Same policy vocabulary, per relationship type or global
  --updated-at NAME[,NAME]  Candidate timestamp properties; when both sides
               carry one, a strictly newer remote row is skipped (counted
               remote-newer), newer-or-equal local applies (equal is
               idempotent), incomparable pairs apply with a warning count
  --rel-mode MODE  keyed (default; merge on the type's resolved key — a
               --rel-key override, else its relationship uniqueness/key
               constraint — falling back to one rel of a type between two
               nodes when neither exists), structural (force the pair even
               when a key exists; parallel rels collapse), create
               (non-idempotent escape hatch)
  --merge-key LABEL:PROP[,PROP]  Merge key for one label, overriding the
               constraint-derived key (repeatable)
  --rel-key TYPE:PROP[,PROP]  Merge key for one relationship type, overriding
               its constraint-derived key or supplying one where no
               constraint exists (repeatable)
  --unkeyed-labels ACTION  skip (default; reported and counted) or create
               (one-shot seeding rows; non-idempotent)
  --dry-run    Print the plan (counts, merge keys, statement shapes, batch
               counts, policies) without touching the remote
  --json       Print the run report as one JSON object instead of the table
  --allow-plaintext  Permit Basic auth to a non-loopback http:// Query API
                     (insecure; prints a warning); default off

Merge keys come from the store's uniqueness and node/relationship key
constraints (composite keys included), overridable per label and per type;
a label with none is reported, never guessed. Nothing is ever deleted
remotely; a failed batch fails the push naming the statement and row range,
and the report lists exactly which batches landed.

  # Push the whole store into an Aura instance, planning first
  relate push --to .env --database ./graph --dry-run

  list      Print each target agent's install state and path

  --agent NAME  Target one agent (default: all detected)

                otherwise refuse it (install: an unmarked, unrecognizable
                dir; remove: any unmarked dir); not valid with list|check

  # Install the agent skill into every detected agent
  relate skill install

Usage: relate run <name> [flags]

Run an installed command-kind extension: the child walks its
source and emits rows over the wire; the host alone owns the store, the
caps and the exit codes.

Installed actions:
  none (relate extension install <name> adds one)

  -d, --database PATH   Database to import into (default :memory:).
                         An explicit --database exits after the import; without
                         it, a TTY opens the shell on the in-memory graph.

An uninstalled name fails closed with the discovery error — nothing is
fetched; the flags an action accepts are its own
manifest's flag table.

Examples:
  # Run an installed action into a store the host owns
  relate run greet ./src -d ./graph

Usage: relate serve --database PATH [--host HOST] [--http PORT] [--origin ORIGIN] [--mcp PORT|stdio] [--bolt PORT [--bolt-identity STRING] [--ws-allow-origin ORIGIN] [--ws-max-connections N]] [--read-only[=FRESHNESS]] [--load SOURCE] [--auth USER:PASSWORD] [--concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE] [--max-traversal-depth N] [--expression-memory-limit SIZE] [--safe | --no-safe] [--logical-graph-size-limit SIZE] [--durability-mode MODE] [--snapshot-format F]

serve hosts Relate's network surfaces on one open database until
SIGINT/SIGTERM. At least one surface flag is required; ports
have no defaults, and a taken port is a startup error.
  -d, --database PATH  The store to serve (directory, .rl bundle, or :memory:)
  --host HOST    Bind host for every served surface. Default
                       127.0.0.1 (loopback only). Any other host deliberately
                       exposes the PLAINTEXT surfaces to the network — serve
                       has no TLS — and a loud WARNING prints at startup
  --http PORT    HTTP Query API v2 endpoint (POST /db/<name>/query/v2; plus the
                       public GET / discovery document) on --host:PORT
  --origin ORIGIN  Allow a browser Origin on the HTTP surface (repeatable;
                   an exact URL or * for any). Default: loopback origins plus
                   https://browser.neo4j.io and https://console.neo4j.io
  --tx-idle-timeout-secs N
                   Expire an HTTP managed transaction after N seconds idle; the
                   next registry operation sweeps it. Default:
                   RELATE_TX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS, else 60. 0 disables expiry
  --max-open-transactions N
                   Cap on open HTTP managed transactions. Over cap
                   is a typed 429 naming this flag. Default:
                   RELATE_MAX_OPEN_TRANSACTIONS, else 128. 0 is unlimited
  --mcp PORT|stdio
                   MCP server: PORT serves the streamable HTTP transport
                   on --host:PORT; the `stdio` keyword serves the stdio
                   transport in the foreground (newline-delimited JSON-RPC
                   on stdin/stdout, for MCP hosts) until the host closes
                   stdin — no auth challenge
  --bolt PORT    Bolt server (Bolt + Bolt-over-WebSocket) on --host:PORT.
                   WebSocket Origins default to loopback (any port) plus the
                   hosted Neo4j Browser and Neo4j Console; another Origin
                   needs --ws-allow-origin
  --ws-allow-origin ORIGIN
                   Allow this Origin on Bolt-over-WebSocket upgrades
                   (repeatable; an exact http(s) URL or * for any). Overrides
                   the default: loopback plus https://browser.neo4j.io and
                   https://console.neo4j.io with auth on, loopback only with
                   --auth none
  --bolt-identity STRING
                   HELLO `server` agent string for the Bolt surface.
                   Default: RELATE_IDENTITY, else
                   Relate/<version>. Sent verbatim — a Neo4j-shaped
                   value (Neo4j/5.26.0) admits strict tooling like
                   cypher-shell without claiming feature parity
  --ws-max-connections N
                   Opt-in cap on concurrent WebSocket sessions.
                   Default: RELATE_WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS, else unlimited —
                   bulk data transfers legitimately run many sessions. The
                   process-wide --max-connections cap still applies
  --read-only[=FRESHNESS]  Open the existing store read-only:
                   no writer lease, never creates it; every
                   write fails. FRESHNESS is snapshot (default: a frozen
                   snapshot at open) or live: tail the WAL and
                   follow the writer's commits; refuses .rl and :memory:.
                   Attach the value; once per run
  --load SOURCE   Load the served store's content from SOURCE — a
                   .rl bundle, a store directory, or an https URL — into
                   --database. A :memory:
                   target (the default) turns the source into the
                   in-memory store: read-only, nothing held open or
                   locked, a fetched copy released after the load. A path
                   target creates the store there (the path must not
                   exist) and opens it writable by default
  --auth USER:PASSWORD  Basic-auth credential shared by every served
                       surface; `none` disables auth. Default:
                       RELATE_AUTH, else a generated token printed at
                       startup (persisted as <dir>.auth-token, 0600)
  --max-connections N  Process-wide session cap shared by every surface.
                       Over cap is accept-then-close. Default:
                       RELATE_MAX_CONNECTIONS, else 128
  --header-deadline-secs N
                   Absolute deadline for a complete HTTP/MCP request header
                   block. Trickled headers are dropped at the
                   deadline. Default: RELATE_HEADER_DEADLINE_SECS, else 10. 0 disables the deadline
  --body-deadline-secs N
                   Absolute deadline for a complete HTTP/MCP request body.
                   Trickled bodies are dropped at the deadline.
                   Default: RELATE_BODY_DEADLINE_SECS, else 60. 0 disables the deadline
  --concurrent-logical-workspace-limit SIZE
                       Admit queries against a shared logical-workspace
                       pool (bytes or mb/mib/gb/gib). A positive
                       value turns admission on. Omit, or an unset
                       RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT, leaves
                       it off. 0 is rejected. Same resolution as the query
                       session's flag
  --max-traversal-depth N
                       Largest explicit traversal hop bound a served
                       statement may ask for (1 through 2000). Default:
                       RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH, else 500. An *1..N or
                       {1,N} bound above it fails at admission with
                       TraversalDepthExceeded
  --expression-memory-limit SIZE
                       Per-value expression build cap for the served store
                       (bytes, mb/mib/gb/gib, or none). Default:
                       256 MiB, or raise/lower it here; none disables the
                       cap for known bulk pipelines
  --safe, --no-safe
                       Refuse agent-typical dangerous statement shapes on
                       the served store. Default:
                       RELATE_SAFE_MODE=1/0, else off. --no-safe
                       negates an enabled environment default
  --logical-graph-size-limit SIZE
                       Live graph + index cap for the served store (bytes
                       or mb/mib/gb/gib). Default:
                       RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT, else unlimited —
                       the same resolution as the query session's flag
  --durability-mode MODE
                       Commit durability policy for the served store:
                       full, everysecond, or snapshot. Default:
                       RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE, else full — the same
                       resolution as the query session's flag
  --snapshot-format F
                       Snapshot format for the served store (parquet|json|markdown).
                       Default: RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT (a codec name), else

                  tag or a full 40-hex commit sha. Resolution records the tag's commit
                  and the platform asset's SHA256; a moved tag or changed asset refuses
                  before any fetch unless re-approved

                  source; a non-https URL refuses before any fetch)
  --from DIR     Install the unpacked package directory (local: the directory is the
                  trust act, like pull --from; the executable must resolve
                  inside it)

  --force        Clobber a target directory without the install marker (never a
                  name collision or a tier's own reinstall path)
  --re-approve   With --github: re-approve whatever the pin resolves to now, replacing a
                  recorded pin that moved (the new asset must verify first)
  --approve SHA  With --github: re-approve only the commit SHA the pin resolves to;
                  any other resolution refuses
  list          Print the installed set — name, version, tier, source; offline,
                  dependency-free, never a fetch
  list --available
                  Print the channel's catalog (the signed extensions.json index): one row
                  per package — name, newest version, protocol, installed — hidden
                  packages omitted. Offline it fails closed naming the index URL
  list --trust
                  Print the recorded GitHub pins — name, repo, tag, commit, asset SHA256 —
                  from $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/extensions-trust.json; offline
  remove <name>  Remove the installed package (the provenance marker is required;
                  a foreign or unknown directory is a refusal, and there is no --force)
  remove --forget-pin

                  the package, so a reinstall is still compared against it
  check <dir>   Run a package directory through the mount's six stages — manifest,
                  executable, spawn, initialize, notifications/initialized, tools/list —
                  printing one line per stage, then one on the recorded GitHub pin
                  (approved / drifted / not from a GitHub source; the pin line never
                  changes the exit code). It opens no store, fetches nothing and runs no
                  tool, so it is safe before installing: exit 2 for a manifest or
                  packaging problem, 1 for what the package does when run, 0 when it
                  would mount

signing key upgrade verifies), github-pin (--github: the release's tag, commit
and asset SHA256 are recorded on first install — the invocation is the approval;
a moved tag or changed asset refuses without --re-approve/--approve), third-party
(--url: the invocation is the trust act, the install line names what landed),
local (--from: whoever provisions the directory owns what is in it).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MAX_ROWS
environment_variables.summary: Default row cap per statement; `0` is unlimited; a bad value exits 2.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_SAFE_MODE
environment_variables.summary: `1` turns safe mode on, `0` off; any other value exits 2.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_PREVIEW
environment_variables.summary: Comma-separated preview Cypher features to enable (for example `ontology`, `hybrid-search`); an unknown name fails the open with exit 1.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_SNAPSHOT_FORMAT
environment_variables.summary: Default snapshot codec for an empty directory; on an existing store a different value fails the open (exit 1).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_CHECKPOINT_INTERVAL_SECS
environment_variables.summary: Default timed checkpoint period.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_DURABILITY_MODE
environment_variables.summary: Default commit durability policy: `full`, `everysecond` or `snapshot`; any other value exits 2.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT
environment_variables.summary: Default live graph and index cap; `0` or unset is unlimited.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_EXPRESSION_MEMORY_LIMIT
environment_variables.summary: Default per-allocation expression cap; `none`/`0` disables it.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT
environment_variables.summary: Default concurrent logical-workspace pool; a positive size turns admission on; `0` exits 2.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MAX_TRAVERSAL_DEPTH
environment_variables.summary: Default traversal-depth admission limit, 1 through 2000.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_LOAD_CSV_DIR
environment_variables.summary: Fallback CSV directory when the flag is absent; neither set means local files are denied. An empty or blank value fails the open (exit 1, `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: LOAD CSV invalid configuration`).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_HELP_EXAMPLES
environment_variables.summary: `0`, `false`, `off` or `no` drops the Examples section from every help page.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_AUTH
environment_variables.summary: Basic-auth credential (`user:password` or `none`) for every served network surface; `--auth` overrides it.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_PATTERN_ENGINE
environment_variables.summary: Diagnostic pattern-engine switch: `auto`, `nfa` or `walk`. Not a supported tuning knob.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_BULK_BATCH_THRESHOLD
environment_variables.summary: Estimated touched-entity count at which an eligible global bulk write switches to batched commits.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_BULK_BATCH_BUDGET
environment_variables.summary: Estimated touched-entity budget per batch commit of an eligible global bulk write.

environment_variables.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
environment_variables.summary: Optional bearer token for release-asset downloads; required while the repository is internal.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_RELEASES_JSON_URL
environment_variables.summary: Override the release-metadata URL (dev and test).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_EXTENSIONS_JSON_URL
environment_variables.summary: Override the extension channel-index URL (dev and test).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_RELEASE_DOWNLOAD_URL
environment_variables.summary: Override the base of the direct release-download route (dev and test).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_GITHUB_API_URL
environment_variables.summary: Override the base of the GitHub API asset route (dev and test).

environment_variables.name: NEO4J_URI
environment_variables.summary: Source Query API URI when `--from` is omitted.

environment_variables.name: NEO4J_USERNAME
environment_variables.summary: Source username when `--from` is omitted (`NEO4J_USER` also accepted); for `relate push`, when `--to` is a Query API URI rather than an env file.

environment_variables.name: NEO4J_PASSWORD
environment_variables.summary: Source password when `--from` is omitted; for `relate push`, when `--to` is a Query API URI rather than an env file.

environment_variables.name: NEO4J_DATABASE
environment_variables.summary: Source database name when `--from` is omitted; for `relate push`, when `--to` is a Query API URI rather than an env file.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MIXPANEL_ENDPOINT
environment_variables.summary: Overrides the Mixpanel /track URL (development and testing); https:// for any host, http:// only for a loopback host; a rejected value turns usage metrics off for the run, with one stderr warning.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MIXPANEL_TOKEN
environment_variables.summary: Overrides the compiled-in Mixpanel project token (development and testing).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_TX_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECS
environment_variables.summary: Default HTTP managed-transaction idle timeout.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MAX_OPEN_TRANSACTIONS
environment_variables.summary: Default cap on open HTTP managed transactions.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MAX_CONNECTIONS
environment_variables.summary: Default process-wide session cap.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_WS_MAX_CONNECTIONS
environment_variables.summary: Default cap on Bolt-over-WebSocket sessions.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_HEADER_DEADLINE_SECS
environment_variables.summary: Default HTTP/MCP header deadline.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_BODY_DEADLINE_SECS
environment_variables.summary: Default HTTP/MCP body deadline.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_IDENTITY
environment_variables.summary: Default Bolt HELLO server agent string.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MARKDOWN_BODY_PROPERTIES
environment_variables.summary: The markdown codec's body properties for an open without the flag; a value that does not parse fails the open (exit 1).

environment_variables.name: RELATE_SHARD_TARGET_BYTES
environment_variables.summary: The target Parquet shard size at a checkpoint, 1 to 1073741824. Read at each checkpoint that writes Parquet shards, after the run's statements have committed; an invalid or empty value fails that checkpoint (exit 1). A `:memory:` run, a `--read-only` open and a `json`-codec store never read it.

environment_variables.name: XDG_CONFIG_HOME
environment_variables.summary: When set, non-empty and absolute, the config directory is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/relate/`.

environment_variables.name: HOME
environment_variables.summary: The fallback config directory `~/.config/relate/`, and the base of the agent directories `relate skill install` writes to.

environment_variables.name: COLUMNS
environment_variables.summary: The table wrap width when stdout is not a terminal; a value under 20 is ignored.

environment_variables.name: CI
environment_variables.summary: A value other than empty, `0` or `false` reports the usage-metrics invoker as `ci`.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_MEMORY_LIMIT
environment_variables.summary: Retired: setting it fails the open (exit 1) with `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_MEMORY_LIMIT is set but ignored; set RELATE_LOGICAL_GRAPH_SIZE_LIMIT`.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_TOKEN_ADMISSION
environment_variables.summary: Retired: setting it fails the open (exit 1) with `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_TOKEN_ADMISSION is set but ignored; set RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT`.

environment_variables.name: RELATE_CONCURRENT_PEAK_TOKEN_LIMIT
environment_variables.summary: Retired: setting it fails the open (exit 1) with `Failed to open Relate: semantic error: RELATE_CONCURRENT_PEAK_TOKEN_LIMIT is set but ignored; set RELATE_CONCURRENT_LOGICAL_WORKSPACE_LIMIT`.

get-started/agent-memory.mdx.command:
cat > remember.cypher <<'EOF'
UNWIND $episodes AS m
CREATE (ep:Episode {id: m.id, session: m.session, kind: m.kind, at: datetime(m.at), text: m.text})
CREATE (f:Fact {id: m.factId, text: m.fact, slot: m.slot, validFrom: datetime(m.validFrom),
                recordedAt: datetime(m.at), embedding: vector(m.embedding, 4, FLOAT32)})
CREATE (f)-[:FROM]->(ep)
WITH ep, f, m
CALL (ep, f, m) {
  UNWIND m.about AS key
  MATCH (n:Entity {key: key})
  CREATE (ep)-[:MENTIONS]->(n), (f)-[:ABOUT]->(n)
}
CALL (f) {
  MATCH (old:Fact {slot: f.slot}) WHERE old.recordedAt < f.recordedAt AND old.closedAt IS NULL
  SET old.validTo = f.validFrom, old.closedAt = f.recordedAt
  CREATE (f)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old)
  RETURN count(old) AS replaced
}
RETURN ep.id AS episode, f.text AS fact, replaced;
EOF

cat > recall.cypher <<'EOF'
MATCH (f:Fact)
SEARCH f IN (VECTOR INDEX fact_embedding FOR $vector WHERE f.closedAt IS NULL LIMIT $k) SCORE AS score

       COLLECT { MATCH (f)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(old:Fact) RETURN old.text } AS replaced
ORDER BY score DESC;
EOF

reference/cypher/search.mdx.command:
relate --database ./search.rl "CREATE (ada:Person {name: 'Ada', role: 'engineer', focus: vector([0.9, 0.1, 0.2], 3, FLOAT32), bio: 'Writes the storage engine in Rust'}),
       (grace:Person {name: 'Grace', role: 'engineer', focus: vector([0.3, 0.9, 0.1], 3, FLOAT32), bio: 'Keeps the conformance tests green'}),
       (noor:Person {name: 'Noor', role: 'maintainer', focus: vector([0.2, 0.3, 0.9], 3, FLOAT32), bio: 'Reviews the docs and the tests'}),
       (relate:Project {name: 'relate', language: 'Rust'}),
       (tck:Project {name: 'opencypher-tck', language: 'Gherkin'}),
       (ada)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2024}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2023}]->(relate),
       (grace)-[:WORKS_ON {since: 2022}]->(tck),
       (noor)-[:MAINTAINS]->(relate),
       (ada)-[:KNOWS]->(grace);
CREATE VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR (p:Person) ON (p.focus) WITH [p.role]
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {'vector.dimensions': 3, 'vector.similarity_function': 'cosine'}};
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX person_bio FOR (p:Person) ON EACH [p.bio]"

RELATE_PREVIEW=hybrid-search relate --database ./search.rl --read-only --mode table "MATCH (p:Person) SEARCH p IN (COMBINE (VECTOR INDEX person_focus FOR [0.1, 0.9, 0.1] LIMIT 3 WEIGHT 0.7, FULLTEXT INDEX person_bio FOR 'docs tests' LIMIT 3 WEIGHT 0.3) USING WRRF WITH CONSTANT 60 LIMIT 3) SCORE AS score RETURN p.name AS name, score"
